(3) Claim classes are handled properly. (5) Doctrine is respected. These are pure JSON tools with no DSP, so there is no high-pass or notch default to check. The unknown fields are present: musical_verdict, performance_grade, listening_acceptance, editor_import and picture_coverage. Inputs are read with byte limits (20 MB JSON, MAX_FLAGS 50,000). No path runs a subprocess, so no timeout is needed.

Metric-validity risk (not a blocker): scripts/corpus_eval_s2.py:108-123,247-262 computes per-axis 'recall' with any eligible proposal by kind-agnostic interval overlap. That includes long spectral_texture_region flags, and the rest axis labelled detector_for_axis 'none'. Once there are labelled positives and coverage reaches 0.5, these axes will print numeric recall that is mostly chance overlap, not detection of that error type. It is disclosed in limitations and the detector_for_axis labels, but a consumer could misread it. Consider making recall null when detector_for_axis is 'none', or adding a chance baseline.

Minor inconsistency: in scripts/corpus_eval_s2.py:215, overall metrics use every annotation_v2.KINDS value, including noise, tone, meter_mismatch and other. A quoted, accepted operator_assertion of kind noise or tone would therefore count as a labelled positive in overall recall, even though NOT_SCORED_KINDS says those kinds are 'not a performance axis'.

By frozen design (contract line 90-94), annotation_markers.BASIS_PRIORITY puts operator_context below detector_hypothesis. User-provided INTENT/context rows can therefore be suppressed by detector rows under the 2-callout limit. They stay in suppressed_markers with a reason, and operator_assertion rows are protected. This is worth stating explicitly in AGENTS-facing docs, since AGENTS says user-reported items must stay distinguishable from detector hypotheses.

Non-atomic pair: annotation_markers.write_outputs (scripts/annotation_markers.py:214-216) writes the JSON and then the CSV as two separate atomic writes. If the CSV write fails, a JSON is left without its CSV. Refusals before writing are handled correctly.

The output guards in flags_triage.py:343 and corpus_eval_s2.py:312 only stop output into the input run directory (or the proposals' parent). A different accepted artifacts/runs/* directory is not blocked. This is low risk because the operator supplies the path.

Real-take test thresholds: test_flags_triage.py:248-251 asserts total_flags == 171 and shown <= 30. These are an input-identity pin plus the acceptance bound, not a tuned magic number, and the structural invariants are checked separately. OK.
